title: Cryptocurrency & Blockchain Privacy Security Checklist
metaDescription: Complete security checklist for cryptocurrency privacy, blockchain anonymity, and protecting your crypto transactions from surveillance.
intro: Cryptocurrency transactions leave permanent traces on public blockchains, making privacy protection essential. This checklist covers wallet security, transaction anonymity, and protecting your crypto activity from surveillance and tracking.

items.why: Privacy coins like Monero and Zcash offer built-in transaction anonymization that Bitcoin lacks, making your transactions much harder to trace.
items.howTo: Consider using Monero (XMR) for maximum privacy or Zcash (ZEC) for selective transparency. Exchange some Bitcoin to privacy coins through decentralized exchanges for better anonymity.

items.task: Generate new wallet addresses for each transaction
items.why: Reusing addresses creates a traceable pattern linking all your transactions together, compromising your financial privacy completely.
items.howTo: Enable automatic address generation in your wallet settings. Most modern wallets like Electrum or Wasabi create new addresses automatically. Never share the same address publicly multiple times.

items.why: Hardware wallets keep your private keys offline and secure from malware, hackers, and computer vulnerabilities that could steal your funds.
items.howTo: Purchase a reputable hardware wallet like Ledger or Trezor from official sources only. Transfer your crypto from exchanges to hardware storage and store recovery phrases securely offline.

items.task: Properly backup and secure seed phrases
items.why: Your seed phrase is the master key to all your crypto. If compromised or lost, you could lose access to your funds permanently.
items.howTo: Write seed phrases on paper or metal plates. Store copies in multiple secure locations like safety deposit boxes. Never store digitally or take photos of seed phrases.

items.task: Use Bitcoin mixing services for transaction privacy
items.why: Coin mixing breaks the transaction trail by pooling your Bitcoin with others, making it much harder to trace the original source.
items.howTo: Use mixing services like Wasabi Wallet's CoinJoin or Samourai Wallet's Whirlpool. Mix coins before major transactions to break the trail from exchanges to your activities.

items.why: KYC exchanges link your real identity to all crypto transactions, creating a permanent government-accessible record of your activities.
items.howTo: Use DEXs like Bisq, AtomicDEX, or peer-to-peer platforms. For centralized exchanges, consider those with minimal KYC requirements for smaller amounts.

items.task: Connect through Tor for all crypto activities
items.why: Your IP address reveals your location and identity when accessing crypto services, allowing correlation of your transactions with your real identity.
items.howTo: Use Incognito Browser or Tor Browser when accessing crypto exchanges, wallets, or blockchain explorers. Many privacy wallets have built-in Tor support you should enable.

items.why: Consistent patterns in timing and amounts create behavioral fingerprints that can be used to identify and track your transactions.
items.howTo: Add random delays before sending transactions. Vary amounts by using round numbers less frequently. Spread large transactions across multiple smaller ones over time.

items.task: Use dedicated devices for crypto activities
items.why: Separating crypto activities from daily computing reduces exposure to malware, keyloggers, and other security threats that could compromise your funds.
items.howTo: Use a dedicated computer or phone for crypto that isn't used for email, social media, or web browsing. Keep crypto devices updated and run minimal software.

items.task: Use encrypted communication for crypto discussions
items.why: Discussing crypto holdings or transactions through unsecured channels exposes you to targeted attacks and surveillance.
items.howTo: Use Signal or Element for crypto-related conversations. Never discuss holdings, trades, or wallet details through email, SMS, or social media platforms.

items.why: Companies and governments use blockchain analysis to track funds, identify users, and monitor transactions even years after they occur.
items.howTo: Learn about chain analysis techniques. Use tools like OXT or Blockchair to see what information is publicly visible about your transactions before assuming privacy.

items.task: Always use VPN for crypto website access
items.why: ISPs and network operators can monitor and log your visits to crypto exchanges and services, building profiles of your financial activities.
items.howTo: Use a no-logs VPN service when accessing any crypto-related websites. Choose VPNs that accept crypto payments and don't require personal information for signup.
